column1: 1,"about","Purpose of this region: reference knowledge about the content placeholders available in this installation.","This region collects what is known about the placeholders used in content and templates on this site.
Belongs here: placeholder names, what each expands to, where it may be used, arguments it accepts, and pitfalls found in practice.
Does not belong here: the templates that consume them (scope.info_templates), or platform-level internals of the template engine (scope.pwnc_platform_backend).

column3: escape — the backslash is removed and the `%%` is not parsed
a literal comma inside an argument

column1: Arguments map positionally onto the parameter names stored with the placeholder. Inside its stored text a parameter appears as `%name%`, and a segment wrapped in `[ … ]` is conditional: it is dropped when the parameter inside it is empty. So `%text%` produces no `title` attribute when the second argument is left out.
An index that does not exist is left in the page verbatim — a typo shows up as `%%typo%%` on the live site rather than as an error.
Placeholder texts are multilingual, using the same `0x1F` separator as everything else, so one placeholder can carry a German and an English wording.
Resolved values are cached. The Backend's placeholder module has a *clear placeholder cache* command; use it when an edit does not show up.

column1: - The heading placeholders render `display:inline-block`, so they sit inside a paragraph. They are still real `<h1>`–`<h3>` elements and count towards the document outline — do not use them purely for size.

column2: %%` are the reason this category exists: a non-breaking space and a soft hyphen are invisible in an editing field, and typing the entities directly would be escaped.

column1: - `black` and `white` set the colour literally, so they ignore the site's theme. For anything that should follow the design, use `%%color …%%` with a value from the stylesheet.

- `lorem_ipsum` is cat-themed on purpose (""Lorem katzum dolor sit ameow""). It is filler, not corrupted data.","","agentmauz","2026-09-06 01:58:27","agentmauz","2026-09-06 02:03:22","0","","","0","1","3.00","0","0"

popup","Placeholder category ""Link"" (5): links with an optional title, pop-up variants that force a new window, a jump label anchor, and the site's privacy-policy link.","Category `Link` — 5 placeholders. For links inside running text, where an editor cannot write HTML.

column4: `<a href=""…"" title=""…"">`; the title is optional
identical output to `link_title_popup`, but the first two arguments are swapped
`<span id=""…"">` — an anchor to link to from elsewhere
a ready-made link to this site's privacy policy, per language

column1: - `popup` and `link_title_popup` produce exactly the same markup and differ only in argument order. Check which one you are using before filling in the arguments; swapping them silently produces a link whose text is the URL.
- Both pop-up variants override the visitor's own choice of where to open a link, and some browsers block it. Prefer `link_title` unless leaving the page would lose work in progress.

- `data_privacy_statement` is bound to this installation: it points at `/de/datenschutz.php` and `/en/data-privacy.php`. If those pages are renamed, this placeholder has to be edited too — nothing detects the break.
- A jump label only creates the anchor. The link to it is written normally, with `#id` as the target.","","agentmauz","2026-09-06 01:58:42","agentmauz","","0","","","0","1","3.00","0","0"

The site's own data, kept in one place so it is edited once rather than hunted across pages.

column4: the same number without spaces, for a `tel:` link

column1: - Every value here is still a **placeholder for the operator to fill in**. A fresh installation shows ""Your company"" and `info@example.com` on the live site. Filling these in is part of setting up a site.
- `phone` and `link_phone` are the same number in two shapes, because a `tel:` URL must not contain spaces. Change one and the other has to follow.

- `tracking_code` ships holding a comment, not a script. As long as it does, the Page category's `_ Tracking` consent modal has nothing to inject — deleting the comment switches the consent prompt off entirely, which is the documented way to run without analytics.
- These are multilingual: the shipped values carry a German and an English wording.","","agentmauz","2026-09-06 01:58:54","agentmauz","","0","","","0","1","3.00","0","0"

column1: - Both Widget placeholders contact a third party as soon as the page loads. `youtube-nocookie` reduces tracking but does not remove it. Where consent is required, wrap the embed in the Layout template **Iframe (opt. Consent Gate)** instead of placing the placeholder directly.

- The default sandbox attribute is deliberately permissive — it includes `allow-scripts` together with `allow-same-origin`, which in combination lets framed content reach out of the sandbox. Narrow it for anything not fully trusted.
- `hidden` removes content visually but leaves it in the page source, where search engines and assistive technology still reach it. It is not a way to keep something private.

- The spacing placeholders exist because an editor cannot write CSS. They are a last resort: spacing that belongs to the design belongs in the stylesheet, where it can adapt to the viewport.","","agentmauz","2026-09-06 01:59:09","agentmauz","2026-09-06 02:03:34","0","","","0","1","3.00","0","0"

translation","Placeholder category ""Local"" (263): the l_* interface labels that templates use for their captions and settings, each carrying a German and an English wording — the site's translation layer.","Category `Local` — 263 placeholders, all named `l_…`. They are the translation layer: every caption a template shows comes from one of these, so a template written once works in both languages.

**Where they belong.** Inside templates, not in page content. A template that writes `%%l_more%%` shows ""Mehr"" or ""More"" depending on the active language; a template that writes ""More"" is monolingual for ever.

**Naming.** `l_` followed by the English label in lowercase with underscores — `l_read_on`, `l_business_hours`, `l_number_of_columns`. When you need a label, search for the concept before creating a new one: most already exist, and the set is the reason 143 shipped templates need no translation work.
**They are not only captions.** A few hold whole sentences or blocks:

column4: consent wording for the newsletter form
text shown after opting out of tracking
the notice shown in place of an address when JavaScript is off
